details:
As some of my fellow world-builders may have also noticed, VRChat currently supports Oculus Spatializer which, even by Meta's Standards, is pretty outdated. The Meta XR Audio plugin (https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/unity/meta-xr-audio-sdk-unity/) is becoming more and more widely used because of the benefits in acoustic fidelity that one can gain from how it helps to process sound. 

What all might this allow us creators to do? The potential to create more immersive soundscapes and acoustic journeys within VR would be easier and the end product would be high in fidelity. Some examples of what might be possible, you ask? Sure!

~ High-pass filtering on a telephone sound source without having to put it in audacity.. again.

~ Room correction and treating so those padded cell and empty vacant Sydney Opera house home worlds sound like they should!

~ Voicechangers for pitching sound sources up or down within world. Be the FNAF character your heart desires!

~ Ambisonics that make audio coming from a room sound like it comes from the entryway instead of hearing everything perfectly through the wall like it's your neighbor at 4:00 AM every morning.

I have a pretty deep understanding of sound design from some years of production but that's only matched at how novice I am with the technical side of audio plugins and engines. With that being said, I have no clue how technically difficult swapping audio plugins is but I do that that VRChat is long overdue for something of the sort!

Some of this didn't make sense? Just upvote it anyhow and let VRChat devs sort it out! Thanks for reading!
title: VRChat, I think it's time to upgrade sound plugins
